statement: Late Bronze Age Ugaritic evidence presents El as a senior patriarchal deity associated with leadership of the divine assembly; modern scholarship treats El and the divine council as central features of the Northwest Semitic religious world represented at Ugarit.

sources.citation: Mark S. Smith, The Origins of Biblical Monotheism: Israel's Polytheistic Background and the Ugaritic Texts (Oxford University Press, 2001), ch. 2, “The Divine Council.”
sources.author: Mark S. Smith
sources.access_note: Oxford abstract describes the Ugaritic assemblies of El and Baal and the divine-council structure.

sources.citation: Theodore J. Lewis, The Origin and Character of God (Oxford University Press, 2020), ch. 4, “El Worship.”
sources.author: Theodore J. Lewis
sources.access_note: Oxford abstract identifies El as father/divine kinsman and highlights El's role as head of a mythological divine council.

does_not_demonstrate: This does not mean every biblical use of the common noun 'el' refers to the Ugaritic proper-name deity El.
This does not establish a standalone trans-cultural 'divine council religion' entity.
